subtopics.title: Cost contracts and observable work

objectives.text: Define input size, output size, representation, successful/failed operation and best/worst/expected case boundaries for a reused C algorithm.
Derive and check an exact vector of comparisons, moves, probes or visited edges for original bounded inputs without rebuilding the prior implementation.
Distinguish abstract work, instruction/cycle observations and static control-flow complexity, naming the model and observable required for each claim.

subtopics.title: Asymptotic bounds and finite scaling evidence

objectives.text: Supply positive constants and a threshold proving an upper/lower/tight bound for an original exact cost function.
Derive a multi-parameter bound that includes the chosen input/output sizes and explain why a worst-case claim differs from an all-input bound.
Construct a counterexample to inferring Big-O from a finite measured slope or to interpreting an upper bound as a tight or universal speed ordering.

subtopics.title: Aggregate, accounting and potential analysis

objectives.text: Trace an original sequence on a reused stack/table and distinguish the largest individual cost from a worst-case sequence bound.
Build a nonnegative-credit or potential certificate and check the telescoping total at every prefix, including the declared initial state.
Explain why the amortized guarantee is deterministic rather than a probabilistic average and identify which allocator/copy costs the model excludes.

subtopics.title: From work to instructions, cycles and bottlenecks

objectives.text: Count an executed instruction mix for a reused C/assembly kernel and relate it to a declared weighted-CPI/clock model without assuming one cycle per instruction.
Compute model cycles, dimensional time and a bounded speedup estimate, then compare with target measurements and explain a residual or working-set change.
Produce a multi-measure cost vector including code bytes or branch events and a static connected-function CFG metric without conflating its graph cycles with CPU cycles.

subtopics.title: Storage boundaries and lifetime peaks

objectives.text: Derive simultaneous live, allocated-capacity, retained and scratch peaks from an original timestamped lifetime ledger and reject overlapping/double-counted ownership.
Interpret per-function static/dynamic/bounded stack records and distinguish a call-chain bound, sampled watermark, static sections and process/cgroup resident accounting.
Report space complexity and measured byte categories separately, with target ABI/build identity and unresolved recursion/interrupt/allocator boundaries.

subtopics.title: Block transfers, locality and amplification

objectives.text: Declare N,M,B and fixed-item units for a single-disk external-memory model and trace original sequential/random block references under a specified buffer policy.
Calculate transferred/read/written/useful bytes and an amplification ratio only when its useful-byte denominator is nonzero, retaining cache-layer boundaries.
Compare abstract block-transfer counts with observed syscall/device/bus evidence and explain a warm-cache or buffering discrepancy without equating those layers.

subtopics.title: Component runtime, overlap and completion

objectives.text: Construct a same-clock event ledger for blocking and asynchronous reused components, identifying submit/return/completion and borrowed-buffer release boundaries.
Compute end-to-end latency, throughput and scoped inclusive/exclusive serial attribution while accounting for overlapping phases rather than summing spans blindly.
Interpret elapsed/process/thread CPU observations including process CPU greater than elapsed time, rejecting wall-minus-CPU as a universal waiting measurement.

subtopics.title: Read/write performance and persistence

objectives.text: Trace short transfers, zero/EOF, interruption, nonblocking retry and delayed errors through a reused read/write adapter while counting actual accepted bytes.
Measure bounded buffered read/write and requested synchronization phases separately, declaring cold/warm state, file lifetime and the persistence boundary.
Reconcile component-return timing, file size and device-byte accounting, explaining why successful write, complete transfer and requested durability are distinct evidence.

subtopics.title: Experimental protocol, clocks and uncertainty

objectives.text: Choose and verify an elapsed/CPU/counter clock contract including resolution, adjustment/suspend behavior, integer conversion, wrap and read overhead.
Extend a reused harness with paired repeated consumed-result trials, raw samples, a declared quantile convention, warmup/order controls and an overhead sensitivity check.
Report uncertainty, outliers and observed deadline/jitter/tail statistics without labeling sampled maxima or quantiles as WCET or a universal deadline guarantee.

subtopics.title: Linux PMU counting and sampling boundaries

objectives.text: Record target/kernel/perf/event identity and permitted user/kernel scope for a bounded per-process observation, preserving denied or unsupported outcomes.
Validate grouped raw values and enabled/running times, derive scaled estimates only with positive running time and explain representativeness and counter-ratio limits.
Compare instruction/branch/cache events or sampling attribution with the cost contract, identifying workload, multiplexing and measurement overhead limitations.

subtopics.title: cgroup CPU, memory and I/O accounting

objectives.text: Inspect a permitted cgroupv2 hierarchy/controller/delegation snapshot and distinguish observation files from configuration and inherited restrictions.
Interpret keyed CPU-time/throttle, current/peak memory, per-device byte/IO and pressure deltas with units and scope, retaining per-FD peak-reset and writeback-attribution limits.
Compare a bounded workload with unchanged observations or a prepared delegated quota experiment, explaining quota/pressure effects while preserving an explicit no-root unavailable-controller route.

subtopics.title: Compiler-based profiling and its perturbation

objectives.text: Build matching uninstrumented and instrumented variants of a reused single-threaded component and verify -pg/coverage or entry/exit hook build/runtime boundaries.
Record bounded hook/arc/call or gprof samples and explain inline, recursion/exclusion, dropped-record and caller-dependent attribution limitations.
Compare measured overhead and code/stack effects against the baseline, separating counted execution, sampled self time, estimated children time and off-CPU waiting.

subtopics.title: Bare-metal cycle and timer measurement

objectives.text: Check the selected core/device counter presence, access, enable, processor clock and debug/interrupt conditions before claiming a cycle observation.
Compute a bounded modular cycle delta and clock-unit conversion, reject ambiguous multi-wrap intervals and compare empty-bracket overhead with a reused kernel.
Produce silicon measurements or a clearly labeled captured/static certificate, documenting timer/GPIO alternatives and refusing emulator timing, energy or sampled-tail WCET claims.

subtopics.title: Choosing useful measures and making a performance decision

objectives.text: Select a justified vector of time, latency/throughput, space, work, traffic and code/control-flow measures for an original requirement and explain the omitted observables.
Resolve a case where a faster measured variant increases retained storage, traffic, static test complexity or jitter, using stated acceptance limits rather than a single score.
Submit a reproducible evidence and limitations ledger distinguishing proved model bounds, finite fixture checks, learner runtime observations and conditional energy/hardware evidence.

domains.title: Debugging from symptoms to causal evidence

subtopics.title: Observation, contracts and replay identity

objectives.text: Write an observation record that separates actual output, expected contract, inference and an untested hypothesis.
Reproduce a bounded failure with input, source/image/configuration/environment identities and a finite timeout.
Predict two competing causes and select a discriminating observation before changing the program.

subtopics.title: Build diagnostics, assertions and bounded logs

objectives.text: Interpret warnings and generate a matching debug-information build while retaining the production optimization comparison.
Separate internal assertions from durable external validation and make a bounded diagnostic log preserve the first useful cause.
Demonstrate that disabled assertions or logs do not erase required validation or evaluate diagnostic-only side effects.

subtopics.title: Minimal reproducers and input reduction

objectives.text: Define PASS, same-failure FAIL and UNRESOLVED outcomes with a stable finite replay contract.
Implement a bounded original token reducer using subset/complement trials and preserve the failing input grammar.
Check every single remaining deletion to certify 1-minimality and explain why it does not prove global minimality or causal code repair.

subtopics.title: Stepping, scopes and call stacks

objectives.text: Use source and instruction stepping to stop before the first contract-violating transition in a learner-owned C program.
Select frames and scopes to distinguish the current local, a shadowed name and the caller’s arguments.
Record a backtrace with matching symbols and state what optimized-out or unavailable values prevent it from proving.

subtopics.title: Conditional breakpoints and watchpoints

objectives.text: Choose a pure conditional breakpoint or valid-object watchpoint from a falsifiable hypothesis.
Compare the first observed changed value with the earliest invalid state and account for hardware/software stopping granularity.
Document target width/slot, thread and lifetime limits and choose a bounded alternative when the watch cannot be installed.

subtopics.title: Optimized images, ABI, disassembly and cores

objectives.text: Map a stopped instruction to a source range and explain a missing variable or moved statement in an optimized build.
Check the selected ABI’s preserved-register and frame obligations without treating source stack pictures as a physical guarantee.
Pair a core or saved snapshot with its exact image/symbols and distinguish a stopped state from unavailable execution history.

subtopics.title: Memory fault diagnosis through reused invariants

objectives.text: Locate a bounds, lifetime or initialization contract violation in an isolated learner-owned program using existing T03/T16/T21/T32 artifacts.
Reconcile sanitizer, unsanitized Memcheck and source-level evidence while retaining unsupported or clean-run uncertainty.
Repair the first invalid access or ownership transition and transfer the diagnosis to a changed input without prescribing a UB symptom.

subtopics.title: I/O, errno and descriptor failure histories

objectives.text: Trace positive partial progress, zero/EOF, EINTR and EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK without discarding or duplicating bytes.
Capture errno only after the relevant failure and diagnose EPIPE/SIGPIPE and bounded per-process descriptor exhaustion.
Repair cursor/ownership cleanup under the declared Linux close contract and explain its POSIX.1-2024 portability limit.

subtopics.title: Concurrency, deadlock and lost events

objectives.text: Reconstruct a forced event schedule, happens-before obligations and a wait-for graph while separating mutex correctness from timing observations.
Diagnose a race, deadlock or predicate/wakeup defect using reused T24/T25 programs and whole-thread observations.
Test a causal synchronization repair with controlled schedules and detector runs while leaving unobserved schedules open.

subtopics.title: Bare-metal startup, faults and asynchronous state

objectives.text: Trace the selected F439 reset/vector/startup path and decode a bounded basic exception/fault record using accepted T27/T29/T31 evidence.
Discriminate a bad peripheral setup, invalid stacked state and ISR/DMA ownership defect without blindly reading side-effecting MMIO.
Repair a documented initialization or completion invariant and keep static, emulator and physical-target claims separate.

subtopics.title: Sanitizer, static, fuzz and differential evidence

objectives.text: Select tools for a specified defect class and record their scope, instrumentation perturbation and actual availability.
Generate bounded original inputs and differential checks that compare the same contract and preserve the failing seed.
Triangulate a dynamic report, static alarm and minimized source transition without equating tool silence with correctness.

subtopics.title: Causal repair, regression and delayed blind transfer

objectives.text: Explain a repair in terms of the violated invariant and reject a symptom-only patch with a competing counterexample.
Replay the minimized trigger, adjacent boundary cases and matched debug/release/instrumented builds with explicit observation categories.
Diagnose a delayed unseen variant from an evidence dossier and record remaining claims instead of reusing memorized diagnostic strings.

domains.title: Memory, storage and lifetime failure laboratory

subtopics.title: Controlled observation and detection contracts

objectives.text: Predict which declared detector or invariant monitor can observe an extent, initialization, lifetime or resource defect on a selected path.
Run isolated learner-owned negative and repaired controls with exact build/tool settings and classify observed versus unavailable evidence.
Explain why undefined behavior, native crash details and a clean dynamic report cannot be fixed portable success or failure oracles.

subtopics.title: Object extents, underflow, off-by-one and NUL boundaries

objectives.text: Specify and implement byte-range and string contracts separating capacity, initialized length, signed input index and NUL space.
Locate the first invalid access in lower-bound, upper-bound, one-past and missing-terminator traces before pointer arithmetic or publication.
Repair the contract and verify unchanged outputs on rejection, exact-capacity behavior and a legal-address logical corruption counterexample.

subtopics.title: Checked allocation sizes and integer conversions

objectives.text: Check count, stride, header and terminator arithmetic against the declared representable size limit before each operation.
Distinguish unsigned wrapping, signed undefined overflow and narrowing from an application size-contract violation.
Verify successful boundary allocation and rejection paths with no allocation, mutation or lost ownership on size failure.

subtopics.title: Stack exhaustion, frames and nested execution

objectives.text: Compute a conditional whole-path stack budget from pinned per-function qualifiers, bounded recursion, reentrancy and permitted exception nesting.
Compare that budget with changed-pattern high water and an isolated native exhaustion observation without treating samples as a universal bound.
Distinguish stack-capacity exhaustion from local-buffer corruption and repair depth or frame use while retaining explicit ABI and unknown-frame limits.

subtopics.title: Fixed RAM sections, startup and collision failures

objectives.text: Classify fixed .bss link-region overflow, wrong startup ranges, declared heap/stack collision and stray-write corruption by their distinct first violated invariants.
Derive load/run intervals, aligned fixed section placement and reserved dynamic-region capacity from a supplied synthetic map.
Repair one layout/startup/allocator boundary and verify unchanged retained storage, no overlap and precise link-versus-runtime evidence.

subtopics.title: Leaks, retained storage and failure cleanup

objectives.text: Track each resource acquisition, owning handle, borrowed edge and release across success and every partial-failure prefix.
Distinguish forgotten release, lost owner, indirect lost children and reachable retained storage using a declared finite graph and a separate native leak observation.
Repair cleanup or retention policy and demonstrate exactly-once release, preserved first cause and bounded live and retained byte ledgers.

subtopics.title: Resize, invalid release and stale aliases

objectives.text: Preserve old ownership on failed nonzero resize and invalidate all prior aliases after successful resize even if an address token is reused.
Diagnose double release, interior or foreign release, use-after-free and escaped aliases using a generation/extent history without using invalid C pointers.
Repair ownership and alias publication, test forced failure/movement/address reuse, and explain why free(NULL) or clearing one owner does not repair other aliases.

subtopics.title: Initialization state and delayed invalid use

objectives.text: Separate initialized-field or byte state from addressability, storage acquisition and zero-byte representation assumptions.
Trace the first consumed uninitialized field through propagation to a branch or output and compare supported Memcheck with declared optional MemorySanitizer coverage.
Repair complete initialization and publication, then test different fill patterns, partial failure and field-wise equality without treating padding as semantic state.

subtopics.title: Asynchronous borrowing, DMA and reentrancy

objectives.text: Trace buffer and callback-context ownership through submission, timeout, cancellation request, confirmed completion and reuse.
Reject early reclamation, duplicate or stale completions and reentrant scratch-buffer conflicts under an explicit bounded event contract.
Verify repaired ownership in host histories and separately identify target reachability, ordering, interrupt and device-quiescence evidence required for a physical claim.

subtopics.title: Causal repair, prevention and transfer

objectives.text: Build a competing-hypothesis dossier connecting the first invalid state to delayed crash or corrupt-output symptoms.
Select bounded watchpoint, allocation history, map or fault evidence and state timing, scope and frame-validity limits.
Repair the violated invariant, distinguish mitigation from prevention, and pass unseen capacity, failure, nesting and delayed-completion transfer cases.
